title: Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz Have Priceless Reactions to Australian Open Presenter's 'World No. 1' Blunder - NewsBreak
text:
By Sreeja Banik ,
1 hours ago
Ahead of the 2026 Australian Open, Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz, and several other players participated in the AO 1 Point Slam, which took place at Rod Laver Arena. During the event, the presenter mistakenly confused the world rankings of Sinner and Alcaraz, leading to hilarious reactions from both players.
Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz Hilariously React to Presenter Confusing World Rankings During AO 1 Point Slam In addition to Sinner and Alcaraz, players such as Iga Świątek, Alexander Zverev, Félix Auger-Aliassime, Lorenzo Musetti, Alexander Bublik, Daniil Medvedev, Tommy Paul, Nick Kyrgios, Donna Vekić, Amanda Anisimova, Elena Rybakina, Jasmine Paolini, Maria Sakkari, Belinda Bencic, and Naomi Osaka also competed at the AO 1 Point Slam.
In the second edition of the AO 1 Point Slam, Sinner faced Australian amateur player Jordan Smith. Before the match began, the presenter mistakenly introduced Sinner as the world No. 1 player, when he is actually ranked world No. 2.
The introduction prompted Sinner to smile and glance toward the sideline, where the real world No. 1, Alcaraz, was standing. Alcaraz took the mix-up in good spirits and laughed about it .
The 2026 Australian Open will take place Jan. 12 through Feb. 1 at Melbourne Park, with main-draw matches beginning Jan. 18. In addition to Sinner and Alcaraz, players such as Novak Djokovic, Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud, Andrey Rublev, João Fonseca, Frances Tiafoe, Stefanos Tsitsipas, and Stan Wawrinka are also expected to compete at the Melbourne Major.
This year, Sinner will enter the Grand Slam tournament as the two-time defending champion. In 2025, he was the top seed and opened his campaign by defeating Nicolás Jarry in the first round before overcoming Tristan Schoolkate in the second round. He eliminated Marcos Giron and 13th-seeded Holger Rune in the third and fourth rounds, respectively.
In the quarterfinals, the four-time Grand Slam champion defeated eighth-seeded De Minaur and secured his place in the final by beating 21st-seeded Ben Shelton in the semifinals. In the championship match, he defended his title by defeating second-seeded Alexander Zverev, claiming his second Australian Open title and third Grand Slam title overall. He won his first Melbourne Major title in 2024 by defeating Daniil Medvedev in the final.
Meanwhile, Alcaraz’s best result at the Australian Open has been reaching the quarterfinals, which he accomplished in 2024 and 2025. Last year, he was seeded third and defeated Alexander Shevchenko, Yoshihito Nishioka, Nuno Borges, and 15th-seeded Jack Draper in the first four rounds. His run ended in the quarterfinals with a loss to Djokovic.
